title: Implement many-body energy functional
action: Implement the total energy per ion for metallic hydrogen as a function of crystal structure parameters (lattice vectors, ion positions) and electron density parameter r_s, using the many-body theory of metals developed by Brovman and Kagan (JETP 1967-1971). The implementation must include electron-ion and ion-ion interaction contributions and be capable of evaluating energies for arbitrary crystal configurations at a given r_s.
description: Core computational engine that will be used in the subsequent energy landscape exploration. The agent must implement the theory from the public literature references.

title: Compute energy landscape and output ordering
action: Using the implemented many-body energy calculator, compute the total energy per ion at electron density r_s ≈ 1.7 for the following candidate structures: simple cubic, bcc, fcc, hcp, simple hexagonal, diamond, beta-Sn. For the triangular and square structure families, sample the shear parameter s over an appropriate range and determine the configuration with the lowest energy. Output a single JSON file containing the minimum total energy for each family and each simple lattice.
description: The primary scored artifact whose relative energy values are checked to verify the ordering: triangular family minimum < square family minimum < all other structures.
output_schema: A JSON object with keys 'triangular_family_minimum', 'square_family_minimum', 'fcc', 'bcc', 'hcp', 'simple_hexagonal', 'simple_cubic', 'diamond', 'beta_Sn', each mapping to a float (total energy per ion in arbitrary but consistent units).
